## Radio Theory

production of radio wave: oscillating electrical current and an aerial (antenna)   
electrons moving back and forth in aerial produce changing electrical field   
electrical field moves "away" from aerial at speed of light   
"receiving" aerial induces "identical" current   
amplifiers and filters compensate for power loss of signal at receiving end

transmitter --> transmitter aerial ........ receiving aerial --> receiver --> amplifier -> headset

waves are referred to in terms of frequence or wavelength   
speed of light ~ constant (in vacuum) 300.000.000 $\frac{m}{s}$ = $3 * 10^8 \frac{m}{s}$.
= $162.000 \frac{NM}{s}$

cycles per second = frequency   
doubline frequency will halve the wavelenght, i.e. 2 cycles per second

1000Hz = 1 kHz, 1.000.000Hz = 1MHz, 1.000.000.000Hz = 1GHz

wavelength $\lambda = \frac{c}{f}$

note: for calculations use right units:    
* wavelength $\lambda$: metres
* frequency $f$:        Hz = $\frac{m}{s}$

example: radio signal of 3kHz - find wavelength: $\lambda = \frac{c}{f} =\frac{3 * 10^8}{3 * 10^3} = 10^5m = 100km$

Radio signal has wavelength of 3.5cm. What is the frequency?
$\lambda = 3.5 cm = 3.5 * 10^{-2}m$
$f = \frac{c}{\lambda} = \frac{3 * 10^8 m/s}{3.5 * 10^{-2}m} = \frac{3}{3.5}*10^{10}\frac{1}{s}$
$f = 0.857 * 10 * 10^9 Hz =8.57 GHz$

### Frequency Spectrum

radio spectrum is part of electromagnetic spectrum and covers frequencies from 3kHz to 300GHz.   
spectrum browken down into 8 bands ranging from Very Low Frequencies VLF to Extremetly High Frequencies EHF.

military uses upper VHF and UHF bands for communications.   
civil agencies use the VHF badn from 118MHz to 137 MHz.

Channel spacing now -- in Europe -- 8.33kHz (used to be 25 kHz) ~ increase in number of channels.   
reception (power) usually good when in range

range affected by    
* power of transmitter
* height of transmitter and receiver
* obstracutions between transmitter and receiver.

civil communication is also conducted on HF frequencies between 2.8MHz and 22.0MHz.
These frequencies give long range, over the horizon capbailty
